text:
## Observations

1. Each pair of row and column indices from 1 through 9 identifies one cell, whose value is the product of those indices.
2. The sum is over cells, not distinct values: each cell contributes its product unless that product equals X.
3. The grid always has exactly 81 cells, and each cell’s value can be computed without storing the grid.

## Solution sketch

1. “Each pair of row and column indices from 1 through 9 identifies one cell, whose value is the product of those indices.” Read X, initialize the sum to zero, and visit every pair of indices from 1 through 9, computing its product.
2. “The sum is over cells, not distinct values: each cell contributes its product unless that product equals X.” Add each product that differs from X, then print the sum after all pairs have been visited. This skips every occurrence of X if it appears multiple times and includes all 81 products if X does not appear.
3. “The grid always has exactly 81 cells, and each cell’s value can be computed without storing the grid.” Keep only the running sum and the current indices and product. The algorithm takes O(1) time for the fixed grid and uses O(1) extra space.
